games.brief: Tier A prices the champions firmly: PFF's structural model gives SEA -6.375 off matched unit edges (off/def edges 0.598 each, HFA 3.69) with SEA No. 2 in PFF's post-FA power ranks (10.96 projected wins) against NE's backfilled No. 7, while nfelo says -4.0 with QB adjustments already baked (Darnold -0.09, Maye +0.12 pts, both confirmed starters), blending to a -5.09 core. The TPT spread panel is unrecovered (site blocked); the total panel is a single computer — Dokter Entropy 41.83, clamped per the single-computer rule — sitting 6.7 under nfelo's 48.51, so the 47.0 total core carries low confidence (total sd 4.73). No §5 adjustments were applied: NE EDGE Harold Landry III's A02 roster code is decode-unverified and his WLB3 demotion may be a depth-chart artifact, so he is flagged rather than priced; the Super Bowl LX rematch angle is inadmissible in Week 1, and no verified forecast exists for outdoor Lumen Field. The marquee collisions — NE's No. 1 EPA offense (0.157/play) into SEA's No. 1 EPA defense (-0.111), and PFF's No. 1 NE secondary into Darnold (QB rank 14) — are treated as offsetting and already inside the unit edges. One §6 reallocation: 0.5 points from NE's team total to SEA's on the pace-possession mismatch, SEA running the league's lowest pass rate (52.9%, 32nd) behind its No. 1 defense. The split is not 50/50 because the identity moves 2.55 points to the home side off the -5.09 spread; the pace reallocation adds 0.5 more, landing near SEA 26.6 / NE 20.5.

Tier A reads this as a clear LA edge: PFF's structural model prices LA -4.975 behind post-free-agency power rank No. 1 vs SF's No. 10 (LA: No. 1 DL after the Myles Garrett trade, No. 4 secondary after McDuffie/Watson, 93.6 offense grade — first team in the PFF era to lead both offense and defense grading; SF: OL ~12th with a source conflict, pass rush 20th, coverage 24th), while nfelo sits at LA -2.0 with both QB adjustments already baked (Stafford -0.15, Purdy +0.07 vs team baseline), blending to a core of LA -3.4, total 47.6 on nfelo alone (DVOA diagnostic 46.9). The Prediction Tracker panel is unrecovered for this game — the spread rests on two sources (sd 2.10) and the total on one; that is flagged, not guessed at. No §5 context adjustments were applied: both QBs are roster-confirmed, Week 1 rest is even, the Melbourne Cricket Ground neutral-site HFA is already inside nfelo (-0.18), and no verified forecast exists — the venue's listed roof state is itself unconfirmed. Every premium-position absence was weighed and zeroed: Pearsall (WR, IR) is depth rank 14 behind active Evans/Samuel, Williams (EDGE, questionable) carries an unverified A02 code at SLB4, Dimukeje (EDGE, IR) and McPhearson (CB, IR) are rotational, and Havenstein's absence from LA's W1 roster file is unverified with McClendon at RT1. The team-total split is not 50/50 because the identity moves the -3.4 spread into it (roughly LA 25.5 / SF 22.1), and a further 1.0 is reallocated to LA on PFF's No. 1-graded offense (Stafford QB5, off EPA .149) against SF's No. 24 coverage unit and 52.8 defense grade — the mirror matchup gains nothing against LA's No. 1 DL. Numbers first; the market's 3.5/48.5 was reference only and touched nothing.

Tier A reads one direction: PFF's post-FA power ranks put CHI 15th and CAR 26th (CAR sim 7.01 wins), the structural model prices CHI -0.60 on matching off/def edges of 0.67 with the OL edge forced to 0.0 on missing CAR numbers, and nfelo makes CHI -2.5 with HFA 2.41 and small positive QB adjustments baked in both ways (Williams +0.20, Young +0.12), blending to a core of CHI -1.63 / 45.8 — the total resting on nfelo alone since no PFF total was recovered. The TPT panel is unrecovered for this game (site blocked), so the spread stands on two sources and the total on one. One adjustment was applied: ol_pass_rush_mismatch at +0.75 to CHI on the spread and -1.5 off Carolina's team total, on PFF's statement that the Panthers are "without both Ikem Ekwonu and Taylor Moton, at least to start the year," with rookie Monroe Freeling (No. 19 overall) listed at both tackle spots on the 8/31 depth chart — magnitudes held below ceiling because both statuses are QUESTIONABLE, the A02/A06 roster codes are decode-unverified, and Chicago's pass-rush rank was not recovered. No qb_change: Williams and Young are both confirmed QB1/A01, and nfelo already carries their ratings. The team-total split is not 50/50 because the identity gives CHI the spread's worth of the total, the -1.5 comes entirely off Carolina's side, and a pace-possession modifier moves another 0.5 from CAR to CHI (CHI 2nd in plays/g at 64.5, CAR 23rd at 58.6, per 2025 pbp). Outdoor game in Charlotte with no verified forecast — flagged, no weather number taken.

The Tier-A structural read is thin but consistent: PFF slots TB No. 20 post-free-agency (8.32 sim wins, best in the NFC South) behind a No. 3 OL and No. 15 coverage unit, while no PFF power number was recovered for CIN — the qualitative file gives Burrow the No. 2 QB rank (94.2 passing grade over two seasons) against a defense that allowed the 31st passing success rate in 2025 and swapped Trey Hendrickson (to BAL) for Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. nfelo prices CIN -3.5 with 2.40 of HFA and both QB adjustments baked in (Burrow +0.26 above team baseline, Mayfield +0.09; 538 QB adj CIN +6.45 vs TB +2.22), and the DVOA diagnostic total of 46.17 sits within 0.5 of the 45.76 core. The Prediction Tracker panel is unrecovered for this game, so the core is single-source nfelo on both numbers. No §5 adjustments were applied: both QB1s are confirmed ACT/A01 starters as of 8/31, both rosters are verified clean at every premium position, both teams sit on 7 days, and the outdoor Paycor forecast is unavailable, barring any weather number. No §6 reallocation either — CIN's 29th-ranked defense (0.124 EPA/play) faces a league-average TB offense (0.002), and CIN's Burrow-Chase attack faces an average TB defense, so each mismatch fails one half of its trigger. The team totals are not 50/50 because the identity skews the 45.76 total by half the spread: CIN 24.6, TB 21.1, with no modifier moving that split.

The Tier-A read is one-directional: PFF's structural model makes Detroit -7.731 on a rank-6 power slot (10.6 sim wins, offense 82.8 and defense 81.9 — both 5th, 2025-vintage grades with the season-year ambiguity noted), against a No. 25 Saints team (7.65 sim wins) whose interior DL PFF calls a clear weakness; nfelo lands at -7.0 with HFA (2.41), travel, and both QB adjustments already inside the number (Goff +0.13, Shough +0.15), and the blend prices -7.335. The total is single-source — nfelo 46.271, with the DVOA diagnostic (45.6) sitting nearby — because the PFF total is null and The Prediction Tracker panel is unrecovered for this game (sites egress-blocked). No §5 context adjustments were applied: Shough remains the rated starter with no post-8/31 news, both teams sit on 7 days, and Ford Field is a dome. The lone move is a §6 reallocation of 0.5 points from the New Orleans team total to Detroit's, on Bryan Bresee's IR placement (nflverse week-1 roster snapshot) compounding PFF's interior-DL weakness note against a top-5 graded offense. The split is not 50/50 because the identity already routes about 3.7 points of the 46.3 to Detroit off the spread; the reallocation adds 0.5 on top. Watch item, not a move: both DET starting safeties (Kerby Joseph, Brian Branch) carry decode-unverified A02 codes and depth-chart anomalies — the largest unresolved availability cluster on the slate, flagged rather than priced.

Tier A: PFF's post-free-agency power board has Buffalo No. 3 overall (highest AFC team), Josh Allen its No. 1 QB, and a 2025 team offense grade of 83.3 (3rd); Houston has no recovered PFF power number, but rates No. 2 in PFF's 2026 DL rankings (Anderson/Hunter, the only teammate duo with 90+ pass-rush grades) and No. 2 in secondary rankings, with Stroud just 17th (62.0 passing grade, 34th of 43 in 2025). nfelo prices BUF -1.5 on the road (home WP 0.447) with 1.14 points of HFA and per-QB adjustments already baked (Allen +0.28, Stroud -0.13); no PFF structural spread exists for this game, so the core is nfelo at full weight. The Prediction Tracker panel was not recovered (site egress-blocked): one spread source, one total source, no dispersion estimate. One adjustment applied: total 47.72 to 47.22, a -0.5 §5.1 skill-absence deduction for HOU WR Jayden Higgins (RES/R36 IR, projected top-3 receiver behind Nico Collins; nflverse week-1 rosters + 8/31 depth chart), held at the range minimum because the IR sits at the 8/31 snapshot rather than being fresh news. The spread stands: Houston's elite rush has no injured/weak BUF OT to exploit (Dawkins/Brown healthy, 'strong outside' per PFF), and Buffalo's rush carries no recovered elite rank against Houston's rebuilt OL, so the ol_pass_rush_mismatch category fails its preconditions in both directions. The team-total split is not 50/50 because the identity moves S/2 = 0.75 toward Buffalo and a net-zero ±0.25 reallocation lands the full Higgins deduction on Houston, yielding roughly BUF 24.6 / HOU 22.6. NRG's retractable roof is expected closed for mid-September heat (operational norm, unsourced) and no verified forecast exists, so no weather number was taken.

Tier A prices this BAL -2.0 at Lucas Oil: PFF's post-FA power board has Baltimore No. 4 (Hendrickson signing fixing a bottom-5 2025 pass rush, Lamar Jackson a top-tier No. 3 QB) against a Colts team slotted 21st and labeled boom-or-bust on Daniel Jones' post-Achilles contract, and the structural model converts that to BAL -2.66 (off/def edges 1.12 each way, HFA 2.4); nfelo is milder at BAL -1.5 with HFA 2.397, Lamar +0.4 and Jones +0.03 already baked in, blending to a 2.033 core. The Prediction Tracker panel was not recovered for this game (sites blocked), so the number rests on two Tier-A sources (spread SD 0.82), and the 46.56 total is single-source nfelo with a 46.31 DVOA diagnostic beside it. No §5 adjustments were applied: Jones is the 2026-08-31 depth-chart QB1 with Richardson demoted to QB3 (unconfirmed by presser, flagged, not repriced), all premium starters on both rosters are ACT/A01, the only absences are depth pieces (Lamm, Pinter, Mitchell), and the retractable roof plus absent forecast bars any weather number. Hendrickson-vs-Raimann drew a look for an OL/pass-rush mismatch but Indianapolis returns one of the league's healthiest lines, so it zeroed. The team totals are not 50/50 because the identity split carries the spread: BAL ~24.3, IND ~22.3, with no reallocation modifiers since the only candidates (IND's Keenan Allen-fed pass game vs Humphrey's 900-yard 2025 coverage ledger; pace) rest on 2025-only qualitative evidence. Number first, and the number is the core: BAL -2.0, 46.5.

Tier A is thin but one-directional: PFF has no rank or rating number for either team, but its qualitative read is CLE #28-overall territory (brownsnation.com, verbatim) with a 'still bottom-five' offensive line despite four new starters, against a JAX side PFF calls AFC South favorites behind Trevor Lawrence — the NFL's highest-graded QB from Week 13 of 2025 through the playoffs. nfelo prices it JAX -7.5 (home WP 0.741) with HFA of 1.777 and QB adjustments already baked (Lawrence +0.15, Watson -0.35); 2026 DVOA projections (JAX +0.053, CLE -0.255) and the DVOA total diagnostic (45.3 vs nfelo's 45.9) corroborate the direction. The Prediction Tracker panel was not recovered for this game — spread and total are single-source nfelo, n=1 each. One §5 adjustment was applied at minimum range: ol_pass_rush_mismatch, -0.5 on the spread toward Jacksonville and -1.0 off the Cleveland team total, on PFF's bottom-five OL call plus rookie LT Spencer Fano's debut against active Josh Hines-Allen/Travon Walker and a defense 5th in 2025 EPA/play — producing JAX -8.0 / 44.9. The team-total split is not 50/50 because the identity (T/2 ± S/2) hands the 8-point spread to the home side: JAX ~26.5, CLE ~18.5, with no further reallocation. Open items that were flagged rather than priced: Watson is depth-chart-confirmed only (no independent corroboration; Sanders QB2), Owusu-Koramoah's PUP status is a decoded reserve code, the Garrett-to-LA roster fact raises the risk that 2025-based CLE defensive ratings run hot, and no verified forecast exists for this outdoor Jacksonville kick.

Tier A prices this a field-goal home edge: the PFF/structural model makes PIT -3.19 (off and def edges 0.175 each, HFA 2.4, OL edge uncomputable at 0.0), with PFF power ranks ATL 22 (7.36 sim wins) against a weakly sourced PIT ~19, and nfelo lands at -3.0 with HFA (2.40) and per-QB points (Rodgers +0.56, Tua +0.18) already baked in — both starters confirmed on the 8/31 depth charts, Rodgers reuniting with new HC Mike McCarthy, Tua over Penix in Atlanta. The Prediction Tracker panel was not recovered for this game (site blocked), so the blend runs on two spread sources and a single total source, nfelo's 45.8 (DVOA diagnostic 45.3 corroborates). One adjustment was applied, at the floor of its range: PFF's No. 3 pass rush (Watt/Herbig/Highsmith) against an ATL offensive line PFF calls "one of the worst units in the NFL" — a mismatch the structural core demonstrably could not price (ol_edge 0.0) — moves the spread -0.5 toward Pittsburgh and takes -1.0 off Atlanta's team total, producing PIT -3.6 and 44.8. Every other absence was weighed and zeroed: Jalon Walker (IR) and the Pearce suspension are already inside PFF's 32nd-ranked ATL rush, and the Joey Porter Jr. and Billy Bowman Jr. PUP designations rest on an unofficial A02 decode with no injury reports yet filed, so they are flagged rather than priced. The team-total split is not 50/50 because the identity already hands the 3.6-point spread to Pittsburgh's side (roughly 24.2 / 20.6), and the -1.0 cut sits on Atlanta's total; no §6 explosive-play, red-zone, or pace evidence justified further reallocation. Outdoor game with no verified forecast — flagged, not adjusted.

Tier A is thin and one-sided in sourcing: PFF ranks the Jets 32nd — last — in its post-free-agency power rankings with a 17th-ranked OL (Fashanu-Membou tackles) but sub-65.0-graded edges and a secondary that recorded zero interceptions in 2025, while Tennessee has no recovered PFF power or unit rank numbers — only qualitative reads of a bottom-5 OL outside Peter Skoronski and an elite interior rush built on Jeffery Simmons (91.4 pass-rush grade, 1st-team All-Pro 2025). nfelo makes it TEN -2.5 (home WP .587) with HFA of 1.761 and near-zero QB adjustments (Ward +0.03, Smith -0.09) already inside the number; both 2025 offenses were bottom-3 by EPA/play (NYJ -0.124, TEN -0.148) and the DVOA diagnostic total (44.99) sits within 2 points of the nfelo total (43.19). The TPT panel is unrecovered for this game, so both cores ride nfelo at weight 1.0 with no dispersion estimate. No §5 adjustments were applied: every rank-1 player at QB/OT/WR/EDGE/CB/S on both sides is ACT/A01 on the week-1 file, Geno Smith and Cam Ward are confirmed starters on the 2026-08-31 depth charts, both teams sit on 7 days rest, and the outdoor Nissan Stadium kick has no verified forecast — flagged, not priced. The Simmons-vs-NYJ-interior angle was weighed and zeroed because the mismatch category requires a weak or injured tackle and the Jets' tackles are the strength of their line. No §6 reallocation cleared its evidence bar either, so the team-total split is pure identity: the -2.5 spread pushes TEN to roughly 22.8 and NYJ to 20.3 rather than 21.6 apiece. Card ships at the unadjusted core: TEN -2.5, total 43.2.

PFF's structural read makes this LAC -10.0 on matched offensive and defensive unit edges (1.697 each, HFA 2.4), consistent with its post-FA power gap — LAC No. 8 vs ARI No. 31 — and unit ledger (LAC OL 12th and Herbert PFF QB7 vs ARI OL 22nd); nfelo lands -7.5 with 2.397 HFA and QB starters baked in (Herbert +0.02 pts, Brissett -0.45 pts — the Kyler Murray-to-MIN downgrade is already inside the rating at -11.31 Elo). The blend prices LAC -8.66; the total is 44.7 on nfelo alone, with no PFF or TPT total (DVOA diagnostic 45.9 as a sanity check). The Prediction Tracker panel is unrecovered for this game, so the spread rests on two Tier-A sources with a 1.79-point spread SD. No §5 adjustments were applied: both confirmed starters are already priced, every rank-1 premium player on both rosters is ACT, LAC's lone notable absence (C Tyler Biadasz, IR) is interior OL with both tackles healthy and no OT-mismatch trigger, and the SoFi dome removes weather. No §6 reallocation either — the bundle carries no explosive-play or red-zone evidence, and both teams ran top-7 pace in 2025, so there is no possession mismatch to move. The team-total split is therefore not 50/50 only because the identity pushes the full -8.66 spread through it: roughly LAC 26.7, ARI 18.0.

Tier A is unusually tight and uniformly grim: PFF's structural model makes it LV -3.65 off two bottom-tier rosters (PFF power ranks LV 29 vs MIA 30, OL ranks 24 vs 27, off/def edges +0.133 LV, ol_edge 0.0, HFA 3.05), and nfelo lands at LV -3.5 with the QB gap already baked in — Kirk Cousins at +0.89 pts over LV's baseline against Malik Willis at -0.29 atop a torn-down Miami roster. The 0.541/0.459 blend yields a core of LV -3.57 (nfelo home WP 0.621) and a total of 44.19 carried by nfelo alone, PFF publishing no total (the 45.1 DVOA diagnostic is corroborative only). The TPT panel is unrecovered for this game — the two-source spread (sd 0.104) stands without a consensus check. No §5 adjustments were applied: both QBs are confirmed, MIA's PUP/reserve entries are depth corners and a swing tackle rather than starters, the Crosby-vs-Miami-line angle fails the injured-OT test with the 27th-ranked OL already priced in the PFF core, and Allegiant Stadium is a dome. No §6 reallocation either — both teams sit in the identical slowest pace tier (55.4 plays/g) and neither 2025 offense (MIA -0.022, LV -0.192 EPA/play, 32nd) profiles as explosive. The team-total split is therefore pure identity, 44.19/2 ± 3.57/2 → LV 23.9 / MIA 20.3 — not 50/50 because the spread alone skews it.

Core: MIN -0.9, total 46.8. The Tier-A engines split hard: nfelo prices MIN -3.0 with 1.60 of HFA and a +1.25-point QB uplift for Kyler Murray (largest Elo QB boost on the slate, per nfelo) already baked in, while the PFF/structural z-model reads GB -1.5 on matched off/def edges (-0.845 each) — consistent with PFF ranking GB No. 5 post-FA (9.92 sim wins, Love a top-6 QB) against MIN at 18 (8.41), even as MIN's 2025 defense was elite (3rd in EPA/play) and its offense bottom-5 (28th). The TPT panel is unrecovered for this game (sites egress-blocked), so the spread rests on two sources (SD 3.18) and the total on one — nfelo's 46.81, with the DVOA diagnostic (46.10) as the lone cross-check. No §5 adjustments were applied: Micah Parsons' expected Week 1 PUP absence is already conditioned into PFF's 27th-ranked GB pass rush and was never credited by nfelo's 2025-based rating, and Murray is depth-chart QB1/ACT with no post-8/31 news to price — his confirmation is a flag, not a number. Weather is nil under the U.S. Bank Stadium roof. Team totals split by identity alone — MIN 23.9 / GB 22.9 off the -0.935 spread — with no reallocation, since both teams rank bottom-7 in pace and the bundle carries no explosive-play or red-zone-specific edge for either side.

Tier A: nfelo prices PHI -4.5 (home WP .654) with HFA 0.976 and both starter QB adjustments already baked in (Daniels +0.15, Hurts +0.10); the structural read is one-sided at the trenches - PFF has PHI's OL No. 2 and DL No. 4 against a PFF-verbatim WAS OL No. 32, the sharpest unit mismatch on the Week 1 slate - while 2025 EPA locates the other gap at Washington's 31st-ranked defense (0.152 allowed vs PHI -0.05), and PFF grades both QBs mid-pack (Hurts 15, Daniels 12). No PFF spread was recoverable and the TPT panel is unrecovered for this game, so both cores are single-source nfelo (spread and total n=1 each). One adjustment applied: ol_pass_rush_mismatch at the range floor - spread -0.5 toward PHI (to -5.0) and -1.0 off the total charged to the WAS side (46.5 to 45.5) - held to the floor because the OL-32 rank conflicts with WAS 2025 line performance (4th in rush ypg, top-10 time-to-pressure) and PHI's starting EDGE Jonathan Greenard carries an A02/PUP code of unofficial decode, per spec weak evidence. Both QBs are confirmed QB1 (ACT/A01), so no qb_change, and the A.J. Brown-to-NE departure predates the 8/31 rating date, so it is not an eligible absence. No Section 6 reallocation: both offenses are bottom-third pace and the bundle carries no explosive-play or red-zone-specific evidence. The team-total split is not 50/50 because the identity shifts S/2 of about 2.5 points onto Philadelphia at -5.0, with the pass-rush total hit further debiting Washington's side. Outdoor at Lincoln Financial Field with no verified forecast - flagged, no numeric weather move.

Tier A makes Dallas a short road favorite in this SNF divisional opener: the PFF structural read has DAL edges on both offense and defense (-0.47/-0.47, HFA 0.34) for +1.8, with DAL 16th in PFF's post-FA power rankings against NYG at 24, and nfelo adds +1.0 with QB context baked in (Prescott +0.21 above DAL baseline, second-year Dart -0.13 below NYG's), blending to NYG +1.4. The TPT computer panel is unrecovered for this game — no consensus spread or total — so the 45.5 total rests on nfelo alone, with the DVOA diagnostic (45.7) in agreement. No §5 context adjustments were applied: both QBs are confirmed ACT/A01 as of 8/31, NYG's pass rush ranks only 21st by PFF and fails the elite bar against LT Tyler Guyton's 57.5 grade, both teams sit on 7 days rest, and the outdoor MetLife night kick has no retrievable forecast, so no numeric weather move is permitted. The lone listed absence, NYG rotational DL Roy Robertson-Harris (RES/R36, depth rank 5, code not decodable), was zeroed as non-premium. The team-total split is not 50/50 because the identity assigns DAL T/2 + S/2 as the favorite, and a §6 reallocation shifts a further +1.0 to DAL and -0.5 off NYG: Dallas ran the league's fastest offense (64.9 plays/g) at 0.111 EPA/play with PFF's No. 8 QB, while the Giants' defense ranked 27th in EPA/play and PFF calls the secondary "practically the same underwhelming group." Flags for Appendix C: missing TPT panel, no 2026 PFF power rating for NYG (rank via secondary snippet only), NYG OL rank is 2025-final vintage, undecodable reserve codes, and no weather forecast.
games.brief_problems: All figures verified against the bundle (PFF edges -0.47/-0.47 + HFA 0.34 -> +1.8; nfelo +1.0 with QB adjs +0.21/-0.13; blend NYG +1.4; total 45.5 nfelo-only with DVOA 45.7; ranks 16/24; Guyton 57.5; NYG DL 21st; rest 7/7; RRH RES/R36 depth rank 5; DAL 64.9 plays/g at 0.111 EPA; NYG 27th EPA defense; spread_sd 0.549, n=2). Two required edits: (1) the sentence 'a §6 reallocation shifts a further +1.0 to DAL and -0.5 off NYG' must become the corrected zero-sum +0.5/-0.5 pair; (2) same fix in origin_note and tt_split_note, whose 'game total unchanged' claim contradicted the +1.0/-0.5 pair as proposed.

games.brief: The Tier-A read makes this a near coin-flip: PFF's post-FA power board has Denver 12th and Kansas City 13th, and the structural model prices it -0.08 to KC off offsetting unit edges — DEN brings PFF's #1 OL, #3 secondary, and the NFL's 2025 sack leaders (68; Bonitto 81 pressures, Zach Allen 83) against KC's #7 OL and #4-ranked Mahomes, while Nix sits 19th on PFF's QB board. nfelo is only slightly friendlier to the hosts at -1.0, with 0.34 of HFA and a +0.58 Mahomes QB adjustment already inside that number despite his ACL+LCL rehab (cleared July, zero preseason snaps, confirmed Week 1 starter per Schefter); the blend lands KC -0.58, total 47.4 on nfelo alone since no PFF or TPT total was recovered. The Prediction Tracker panel is unrecovered for this game — the card rests on two spread sources and a single total source, with the DVOA diagnostic (46.5) within a point as the only cross-check. No §5 adjustments were applied: the Mahomes situation is pre-dataset and priced, KC's two roster flags (OT Waletzko RES/R34, DT Norman-Lott A02) are depth pieces with partially undecodable status codes, and the outdoor Monday-night forecast is unavailable, barring any weather number. No §6 reallocation cleared the evidence bar either — no red-zone or explosive-play data exists in the bundle — so the team-total split is purely the identity: the -0.58 spread tilts it to roughly KC 24.0, DEN 23.4 rather than 50/50.
